title: Ginkgolide B Extends Healthspan and Lifespan Through Neuronal NAD+ Restoration and Mitochondrial Proteostasis
abstract: Ginkgolide B, a terpenoid from Ginkgo biloba, extends both healthspan and lifespan in aged mice by restoring neuronal NAD+ levels, enhancing mitochondrial proteostasis, and reducing oxidative stress. Treatment starting at 18 months of age increased median lifespan by 23% and improved cognitive performance, neuromuscular strength, and immune function.

sections.Research Question: Can Ginkgolide B extend both healthspan and lifespan in aged mammals through restoration of neuronal NAD+ metabolism and mitochondrial proteostasis, and what are the molecular mechanisms mediating these effects? This study investigated whether Ginkgolide B could serve as a geroprotective compound when administered to aged mice, addressing whether healthspan and lifespan extensions can be achieved simultaneously with pharmacological intervention in already-aged organisms.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, SciFinder, and Google Scholar for studies of Ginkgolide B, Ginkgo biloba extract, NAD+ metabolism, mitochondrial proteostasis, aging, cognitive function, and lifespan.

sections.Key Findings: Ginkgolide B treatment starting at 18 months increased median lifespan by 23% (p<0.001) and maximum lifespan by 18%. [bundle:1] Cognitive performance on Morris water maze improved (escape latency reduced from 42s to 24s, p<0.01). [bundle:2] Neuronal NAD+ levels in hippocampus were restored to young levels (3.2-fold increase vs. [bundle:3] aged controls, p<0.001), and SIRT1 activity was increased by 2.8-fold. [bundle:4]
sections.Limitations: The mechanistic link between PAF receptor antagonism and NAD+ restoration was not fully established. Human equivalent dosing calculations are complicated by pharmacokinetic differences.
sections.Gaps Identified: Human clinical trials of Ginkgolide B in older adults with cognitive complaints are urgently needed. The upstream mechanism connecting PAF receptor antagonism to NAD+ restoration requires molecular.
sections.Conclusion: Ginkgolide B extends both healthspan and lifespan in aged mice through a mechanism requiring neuronal NAD+ restoration and subsequent activation of mitochondrial proteostasis and sirtuin signaling. The discovery that NAD+ restoration is the critical mediator provides a mechanistic foundation for human trials.

title: Liberal versus Restrictive Transfusion Thresholds in High-Cardiac-Risk Patients Undergoing Non-Cardiac Surgery: The TOP Trial
abstract: The TOP trial randomized 5,243 high-cardiac-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery to liberal (Hb<9 g/dL) or restrictive (Hb<7 g/dL) transfusion strategies. Primary composite outcome of mortality, MI, or stroke at 30 days occurred in 11.4% vs 11.8% (diff -0.4%, 95% CI -2.0% to 1.2%), establishing non-inferiority of restrictive strategy.

sections.Research Question: Is a restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb<7 g/dL) non-inferior to a liberal threshold (Hb<9 g/dL) for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in high-cardiac-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery? This pragmatic multicenter RCT addressed whether liberal transfusion practices that have predominated in high-cardiac-risk surgical patients provide outcome benefits.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing
sections.Search Summary: A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and clinical trial registries for randomized trials comparing liberal versus restrictive transfusion thresholds in surgical patients.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Liberal transfusion strategies have historically been favored in high-cardiac-risk patients based on physiologic reasoning about oxygen delivery. Prior trials in different populations—including critically ill ICU patients—have generally supported restrictive.
sections.Key Findings: Primary composite outcome occurred in 11.4% liberal vs 11.8% restrictive (absolute diff -0.4%, 95% CI -2.0% to 1.2%, p=0.62 for non-inferiority) [bundle:1]. Mortality was 4.2% vs 4.5%, MI 6.1% vs 5.8%, stroke 2.3% vs 2.5%. Liberal group received significantly more transfusions (mean 2.1 vs 0.8 units, p<0.001) with higher transfusion reactions (3.1% vs 1.2%, p<0.001) and TACO (1.8% vs 0.6%, p=0.001).
sections.Limitations: Hemoglobin thresholds were implemented by treating clinicians rather than protocol-mandated triggers. Patients with acute coronary syndrome or emergency surgery were excluded.
sections.Gaps Identified: Comparative effectiveness in emergency surgery and acute coronary syndrome populations requires dedicated trials. Cost-effectiveness analyses would inform health system implementation.
sections.Conclusion: A restrictive transfusion threshold is non-inferior to a liberal threshold for major adverse cardiovascular events in high-cardiac-risk patients, while significantly reducing transfusion exposure and complications. These findings support adoption of restrictive strategies as standard of care.
sections.Methods: A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and clinical trial registries for randomized trials comparing liberal versus restrictive transfusion thresholds in surgical patients.

title: Targeted Capillary Refill Time-Guided Resuscitation versus Usual Care in Early Septic Shock: The ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 Trial
abstract: In 4,220 patients with early septic shock, a personalized hemodynamic resuscitation strategy targeting capillary refill time (CRT) normalization was compared to usual care. 28-day mortality was 31.4% vs 34.3% (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.99, p=0.03), a statistically significant reduction with the CRT-targeted intervention.

sections.Research Question: Does a resuscitation strategy targeting normalization of capillary refill time, compared to usual care lactate clearance targets, reduce mortality in patients with early septic shock? This pragmatic multicenter RCT across 85 ICUs in 18 countries compared a peripheral perfusion-targeted algorithm against sepsis guideline-based usual care.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing
sections.Search Summary: Literature was searched in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase for randomized trials of hemodynamic resuscitation strategies in septic shock.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines recommend lactate clearance and optional ScvO2 monitoring. However, the ScvO2 target has been removed from mandatory recommendations after EGDT benefits were not consistently replicated.
sections.Key Findings: Targeting CRT normalization resulted in lower 28-day mortality (31.4% vs 34.3%, HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.99, p=0.03) [bundle:1]. Intervention group received less fluid in first 6 hours (median 25 vs 30 mL/kg, p<0.001). Organ dysfunction-free days were higher (median 14 vs 11 days, p<0.001). RRT was required in 18.2% vs 21.7% (p=0.01).
sections.Limitations: Intervention was necessarily unblinded. CRT measurement was not standardized with video assessment. The 6-hour enrollment window may have excluded patients presenting beyond this window.
sections.Gaps Identified: The finding of differential benefit by shock phenotype requires mechanistic investigation. Economic evaluation comparing CRT-guided versus lactate-guided resuscitation costs would inform implementation.
sections.Conclusion: CRT-guided resuscitation significantly reduces 28-day mortality compared to usual care in early septic shock, particularly in patients with hyperlactatemia and warm shock physiology. The intervention is low-cost and non-invasive and reduces unnecessary fluid administration.
sections.Methods: Literature was searched in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase for randomized trials of hemodynamic resuscitation strategies in septic shock.

title: Sodium Bicarbonate Therapy for Severe Metabolic Acidemia Complicating Acute Kidney Injury: The BICARICU-2 Randomized Trial
abstract: In 1,122 patients with severe metabolic acidemia (pH<7.20) and acute kidney injury, sodium bicarbonate infusion reduced death, RRT, or persistent renal dysfunction at 90 days (38.2% vs 44.6%, RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.96, p=0.01). Mortality benefit was driven by reduced 28-day mortality (22.1% vs 27.8%, p=0.02).

sections.Research Question: Does sodium bicarbonate infusion to correct severe metabolic acidemia in critically ill patients with AKI reduce mortality and kidney failure compared to usual care without alkalinizing therapy? This multicenter RCT in 78 ICUs enrolled patients with pH<7.20 and AKI KDIGO stage 2-3.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing available evidence from Complementary analyses probe whether effect sizes vary by study design, measurement approach, or sample characteristics.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and clinical trial registries was conducted for randomized trials of sodium bicarbonate or alkali therapy in metabolic acidosis. No language restrictions were applied.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Metabolic acidosis is common in critically ill patients with AKI and is independently associated with mortality. Sodium bicarbonate is widely used but high-quality trial evidence for mortality benefit is lacking.
sections.Key Findings: Sodium bicarbonate achieved the primary composite outcome in 38.2% vs 44.6% (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.96, p=0.01) [bundle:1]. 28-day mortality was 22.1% vs 27.8% (p=0.02). RRT was required in 18.4% vs 21.9% (p=0.08). Time to pH>7.30 was significantly shorter (median 6 vs 18 hours, p<0.001). Adverse effects included hypokalemia (15.3% vs 8.1%, p<0.001) and volume overload (22.1% vs 14.3%, p<0.001).
sections.Limitations: Usual care was not standardized across sites. Volume overload as adverse effect requires consideration in cardiorenal syndrome patients. The mortality benefit was not consistent across all subgroup analyses.
sections.Gaps Identified: Optimal pH target range (7.30-7.35 vs 7.35-7.40) and rate of correction would refine the protocol. The interaction between bicarbonate therapy and concurrent RRT with citrate anticoagulation requires study.
sections.Conclusion: Sodium bicarbonate infusion for severe metabolic acidemia in AKI patients significantly reduces mortality and the composite of death, RRT, or persistent renal dysfunction. Benefits appear to outweigh risks of hypokalemia and volume overload when monitored with protocol-driven potassium replacement.
sections.Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and clinical trial registries was conducted for randomized trials of sodium bicarbonate or alkali therapy in metabolic acidosis. No language restrictions were applied.

title: Rituximab versus Tacrolimus for Maintenance Immunosuppression in Adult Relapsing Nephrotic Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: In 184 adults with relapsing minimal change disease or FSGS, rituximab was non-inferior to tacrolimus for maintaining remission over 24 months (relapse rate difference -3.2%, 95% CI -8.1% to 1.7%) with a more favorable safety profile including lower rates of new-onset diabetes and nephrotoxicity.

sections.Research Question: Is rituximab non-inferior to tacrolimus for maintaining remission in adults with frequently relapsing minimal change disease or FSGS, and does it offer a superior safety profile? This multicenter RCT compared 24-month relapse rates and safety outcomes between rituximab and tacrolimus in adults with relapsing nephrotic syndrome.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by
sections.Search Summary: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central through October 2025. Included studies were RCTs in adult populations with primary nephrotic syndrome comparing rituximab to alternative.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Calcineurin inhibitors have been standard of care for frequently relapsing nephrotic syndrome but carry risks of nephrotoxicity, diabetes, hypertension, and neurotoxicity.
sections.Key Findings: Fewer patients in rituximab group experienced new-onset diabetes (1 vs 8, p=0.03), nephrotoxicity requiring discontinuation (0 vs 12, p<0.001), and neurotoxicity (3 vs 11, p=0.04). [bundle:1] Renal function declined minimally in rituximab group (-2.1 mL/min/1.73m2) vs tacrolimus group (-8.7 mL/min/1.73m2, p=0.006). [bundle:2] Quality of life improved significantly more in rituximab group at 12 months. [bundle:3]
sections.Limitations: Open-label design introduces potential ascertainment bias. Non-inferiority margin of 15% may be considered wide. 24-month follow-up may be insufficient for long-term safety signals.
sections.Gaps Identified: Head-to-head comparisons with cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate, and anti-CD38 antibodies would define optimal sequencing. Biomarker-guided rituximab retreatment strategies warrant prospective evaluation.
sections.Conclusion: Rituximab is non-inferior to tacrolimus for maintaining remission in frequently relapsing adult nephrotic syndrome with a significantly more favorable safety profile, including preservation of kidney function. These results support consideration of rituximab as a preferred first-line steroid-sparing agent.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Percutaneous Coronary Intervention According to Bleeding Risk: The HOST-BR Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: In 5,122 patients undergoing PCI, dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) duration guided by bleeding risk (shortened duration 1-3 months followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs standard 12-month DAPT) reduced bleeding complications without increasing ischemic events (BARC 2-5 bleeding 4.2% vs 7.1%, HR 0.58, p<0.001; definite/probable ST 0.6% vs 0.7%, HR 0.85, p=0.43).

sections.Research Question: Does a shortened DAPT duration (1-3 months followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy) reduce bleeding complications compared to standard 12-month DAPT without increasing ischemic events in patients undergoing PCI? This open-label RCT assigned DAPT duration based on PRECISE-DAPT bleeding risk score.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing available evidence from multiple sources
sections.Search Summary: Literature was searched in PubMed, Cochrane, and clinical trial registries for RCTs comparing different DAPT durations after PCI. Data from the HOST-EXAM and SMART-DATE trials were reviewed.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Current guidelines recommend 6-12 months of DAPT after PCI, but bleeding risk increases with longer DAPT duration. The OPTIMAL trial and others have challenged the 12-month standard.
sections.Key Findings: Definite/probable ST occurred in 0.6% vs 0.7% (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.53-1.37, p=0.43). [bundle:1] All-cause mortality was 1.9% vs 2.1% (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.65-1.27, p=0.57). [bundle:2] Net adverse clinical events (death, MI, stroke, bleeding) favored the shortened strategy (5.9% vs 8.3%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.58-0.84, p<0.001). [bundle:3] Benefits were consistent across subgroups defined by diabetes, ACS presentation, and lesion complexity.
sections.Limitations: The PRECISE-DAPT score was derived from observational data and its application in this RCT population may have led to more aggressive shortening than in real-world practice. Long-term outcomes beyond 12 months were not assessed.
sections.Gaps Identified: Long-term follow-up at 2-3 years is needed to assess whether ischemic benefits emerge with longer observation. The optimal duration for specific lesion subtypes (bifurcation, CTO) requires dedicated.
sections.Conclusion: Shortened DAPT duration guided by bleeding risk score reduces bleeding complications without increasing ischemic events, supporting a precision medicine approach to DAPT duration after PCI This work advances the field by providing actionable insights and identifying promising directions for future study.

title: Global Greenhouse Gas Emissions Mitigation Potential and Life-Cycle Assessment of Green Hydrogen Projects: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: A meta-analysis of 127 green hydrogen projects found that green hydrogen delivers 71-94% emissions reductions vs grey hydrogen under consequential system boundaries. However, only 34% of projects achieved reported emissions reductions in practice due to high curtailment rates and grid carbon intensity variability.

sections.Research Question: What are the real-world life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions of green hydrogen production, and what production and grid integration factors determine whether reported emissions reductions are achieved in practice?This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing available evidence from multiple sources to establish a comprehensive understanding of the research problem.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic literature search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed LCA studies of green hydrogen published 2020-2025.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Green hydrogen is promoted as zero-emissions, but actual GHG mitigation value depends critically on carbon intensity of electricity used for electrolysis. LCA methodology for hydrogen is contested with different system boundaries leading to dramatically.
sections.Key Findings: Critically, only 34% of monitored projects achieved their reported emissions reductions in practice, primarily due to high curtailment rates and grid carbon intensity variability [bundle:1]. Projects that used dedicated renewable generation with on-site storage achieved reported reductions at 89% rates. Life-cycle methane leakage from grey hydrogen was estimated at 3.2-8.7% of throughput [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: Project-level monitoring data were available for only 34% of projects, introducing selection bias. LCA methodologies varied substantially across studies. Future grid decarbonization would improve green hydrogen performance.
sections.Gaps Identified: Standardized LCA methodology for hydrogen production and use is urgently needed. Independent third-party verification of emissions claims should be required for green hydrogen certification.
sections.Conclusion: Green hydrogen achieves significant real-world emissions reductions when produced with dedicated renewable electricity, but the gap between reported and achieved reductions in grid-connected projects highlights the need for rigorous certification standards.

abstract: We introduce MathNet, a benchmark of 30,676 Olympiad-level problems across 47 countries and 17 languages. State-of-the-art reasoning models achieve 78.4% on MathNet Problem Solving (GPT-5), while embedding models achieve only 31.2% recall for mathematically equivalent problem retrieval.

sections.Research Question: Can current state-of-the-art large language models solve Olympiad-level mathematical reasoning problems at human-expert performance levels, and what are the specific failure modes that limit mathematical retrieval-augmented generation? MathNet evaluated 15 LLMs including GPT-5 and Gemini-3.1-Pro on three tasks: problem solving, retrieval of equivalent problems, and retrieval-augmented solving.This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge
sections.Search Summary: MathNet dataset was constructed from national and international mathematical Olympiad problems from 47 countries spanning 2000-2024, translated into 17 languages.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Mathematical reasoning is widely viewed as a key differentiator of advanced AI systems. Existing benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K, GPQA) have been saturated by current models. Mathematical retrieval for retrieval-augmented education represents an unsaturated frontier.
sections.Key Findings: Mathematical retrieval remained a major weakness: best embedding model achieved only 31.2% recall at k=10 for equivalent problem retrieval [bundle:2]. Retrieval-augmented solving improved performance by 12.1% when a correctly similar problem was retrieved, but degraded by 8.3% when a superficially similar but mathematically dissimilar problem was retrieved.
sections.Limitations: The Olympiad domain may not represent the full range of mathematical practice. Automated scoring of proofs may not capture partial credit. The benchmark does not assess conjecture generation.
sections.Gaps Identified: Developing better mathematical embedding models is a high-leverage research priority. The dramatic performance drop beyond 8 reasoning steps suggests fundamental limitations in chain-of-thought approaches.
sections.Conclusion: MathNet establishes that Olympiad-level mathematical reasoning remains an unsaturated frontier for LLMs, with even the best models achieving 14 pp below human experts. Mathematical retrieval is the key bottleneck for retrieval-augmented approaches.

title: Is Taurine an Aging Biomarker? A Critical Evaluation of Taurine Supplementation Studies and Their Implications for Lifespan Extension Claims
abstract: CAUTION: This topic remains controversial with conflicting evidence. We critically evaluate the evidence for taurine as an aging biomarker and lifespan extension intervention. While preclinical studies show promising results, human trial evidence remains sparse and methodologically heterogeneous. We identify significant gaps in dose-response relationships, biomarker validation, and long-term safety data that preclude strong recommendations.

sections.Research Question: Is there sufficient evidence to support taurine as a robust aging biomarker and lifespan extension intervention, and what key gaps in the evidence base should be addressed before clinical recommendations can be made? This critical evaluation reviews the mechanistic basis for taurine's proposed anti-aging effects and systematically assesses the quality of preclinical and clinical evidence supporting supplementation.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar for taurine supplementation, aging, lifespan extension, and biomarker studies through December 2025.
sections.Evidence Landscape: A highly publicized 2023 study in Cell reported lifespan extension in mice fed taurine supplements, generating significant media attention and public interest. However, critical evaluation of the evidence base has been limited.
sections.Key Findings: elegans, mice, and cell models demonstrate consistent mechanistic pathways for taurine's antioxidant and mitochondrial protective effects [bundle:1], human clinical trial evidence remains sparse, underpowered, and methodologically heterogeneous. A systematic review identified only 8 human RCTs with aging-related endpoints, all with significant methodological limitations: small sample sizes (median n=45),.
sections.Limitations: The mechanistic work in preclinical models is robust, but translational gap to humans is substantial and unresolved. Long-term (>1 year) human safety data for high-dose taurine supplementation are essentially absent.
sections.Gaps Identified: Large-scale, long-term RCTs with validated aging biomarkers as primary endpoints are critically needed. Dose-response studies in humans to identify optimal dosing for biological age effects are lacking.
sections.Conclusion: The gap between preclinical enthusiasm and human trial data is substantial, and major claims in the literature are not yet supported by adequate human evidence. The current evidence base does not support strong conclusions. Further well-powered replication studies and standardized methodologies are needed before definitive judgments can be made.

sections.Evidence Landscape: Single-cell aging studies in primates have been limited by tissue accessibility and cost. Most aging atlases have been built in mice, with limited primate data The field will benefit from continued study.
sections.Key Findings: Cell-type-specific aging programs were identified in each organ, with the most pronounced changes in immune cell populations [bundle:1]. Progressive immune infiltration of barrier tissues (lung, gut, skin) was observed across all animals. Shared epigenetic drift patterns across cell types correlated with chronological age and matched epigenetic clock predictions [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: Captive primate population may not fully reflect natural aging trajectories. Cross-sectional design cannot capture individual aging trajectories.
sections.Gaps Identified: Longitudinal single-cell profiling in individual primates across the lifespan would enable within-individual aging rate estimation.
sections.Conclusion: Primate aging involves both cell-type-specific programs and organism-wide epigenetic drift patterns, providing a mechanistic bridge between mouse aging studies and human aging These results contribute to a growing body of evidence supporting continued investigation and potential clinical translation.

title: TRIALSCOPE: Clinical Trial Simulation from Real-World Data Using Causal Machine Learning for Counterfactual Prediction
abstract: We developed TRIALSCOPE, a causal machine learning framework that generates realistic simulated clinical trial populations from electronic health record data. Counterfactual predictions of treatment effects were validated against 12 completed randomized trials, showing good calibration and high discrimination for treatment responders.

title: Improving Energy Return on Investment Calculations for Green Hydrogen Pathways: A Critical Review and Corrected Methodology
abstract: We demonstrate that conventional EROI calculations for green hydrogen systematically undercount auxiliary energy inputs, overestimating green hydrogen EROI by 30-45%. Corrected calculations show green hydrogen EROI of 3.1-4.8 compared to 5.2-7.9 for grey hydrogen.

title: Discordance Between Creatinine- and Cystatin C-Based eGFR: Clinical Implications and Prognostic Significance - A Critical Meta-Analysis
abstract: CAUTION: This topic remains controversial with conflicting evidence. A meta-analysis of 82 cohorts and 1.2 million participants finds that discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based eGFR is common (28% of individuals have >10 mL/min/1.73m2 difference), associated with mortality risk, but methodological heterogeneity and lack of standardized discordance thresholds limit clinical utility.
